The answer is written per target locale with `strapi.documents(uid).update({ documentId, locale, fields: [], data })` (l. 259-275) after `mergeUnsupportedFields` (json counts as translatable, so the provider's value wins). The docs (docs.strapi.io "Internationalization", AI translations) and the source offer no way to exclude an attribute; `pluginOptions.i18n.localized: false` stops localisation altogether. Measured without the guard: a provider that translates every string emptied the target value (`blocks: []`, `version: "[de] 2.31.0"`); one that translates only prose changed math TeX and code. All block ids, types, URLs, internal-link attributes and footnote notes were sent to the provider.

**Guard (`server/src/utils/ai-localization-guard.js`, `shared/ai-localization.mjs`).**

- Bootstrap wraps two i18n services through the services registry `strapi.get('services').extend(uid, fn)`. It does nothing without them and logs a warning when only one exists. `plugin::i18n.ai-localizations.generateDocumentLocalizations` runs inside an AsyncLocalStorage job context `{ uid, documentId, sourceLocale }`. Inside a job, `plugin::i18n.ai-translations.generateTranslations` replaces every editor value of the payload with `{ magicEditorXTexts: [inline HTML, ...] }` (the `collectSegments` strings, links reduced to `<a href="#mex-link-<n>">`). Block ids, types, tunes, files, URLs, `_mex`, `fieldKey`, internal-link attributes, code, math blocks and table structure never reach the provider. Fields without text become `null`.
- Detection rule for the repair: a Document Service `update` inside a job context, with the same `uid` and `documentId` as the job and a `locale` string other than the job's source locale. Every other write (Content Manager, Content API, "Fill in from another locale", scripts) is left alone. The repair is composed in front of the save middleware in `register.js`, so its result is then cleaned and checked against the preset like any write.
- Repair (`repairLocalizedValue(source, answer, { fieldKey })`): the value is rebuilt from the source-locale value (the clean value the payload was built from, else the stored source draft). Only translated inline strings are taken over, each through `repairInline`: links get the source attributes back (matched by placeholder or href, then in order), inline math keeps the source TeX, and footnotes keep their id and get a repaired note. A string keeps its source text when its links, formulas or footnotes do not match, or when it is not a string, is longer than 20000 characters or is empty. An envelope with a different number of strings keeps all source strings. A full Editor.js answer (no envelope) is read by block id and path. Positional fields keep the target locale's own `fieldKey`, so versions and comments stay attached; without one they take the source key.
- Refusal: when the source value of a field cannot be found (for example more repeatable entries than the source has), the write fails with `ValidationError` `details.code: 'AI_TRANSLATION_UNSAFE'`, with `errors` per field path and no content. Strapi then marks that locale failed in the job and logs the message.
- Audit: event `ai.localize` per field with text (`counts: { segments, translated, kept }`, `meta: { sourceLocale }`, field identity as everywhere).

**Releases readiness (`server/src/utils/release-readiness.js`).** `@strapi/content-releases` `server/utils/index.js` `isEntryValid` (l. 46-73) marks an entry ready when `strapi.entityValidator.validateEntityCreation(model, entry, { isDraft: false })` passes. The core validator maps `json` to `yup.mixed()` (`@strapi/core` `services/entity-validator/validators.js` l. 360) and has no custom field hook. Proven before the change: an entry the publish guard refuses (`QUALITY_GATE`) showed as ready, and publishing the release then failed as a whole (`services/release.js` l. 297 calls `documents.publish`, the publish guard throws and the release is marked `failed`). The plugin now wraps `validateEntityCreation`, one object shared by every Strapi instance in the process (`Strapi.js` l. 229), and restores it in `destroy`. For draft-and-publish types with `isDraft: false`, after Strapi's own validation, it runs `blockingIssues` of the publish guard and throws the same `ValidationError` `QUALITY_GATE`. Only guarded fields and only `error` issues count; warnings such as alt hints never block, and drafts are never checked.

- Effects: Releases show such entries as "Not ready to publish" and as ready after the fix (proven in-process with the Releases functions `getDraftEntryValidStatus`/`isEntryValid`). `documents(uid).create/update({ status: 'published' })` (Content API `?status=published`) publishes through the repository without the `publish` middleware (`services/document-service/repository.js` l. 297-309). Such writes were not checked before; they are now refused and rolled back. A normal publish runs the check twice with the same result.
- Not included: preset violations (`PRESET_VIOLATION`, and `ALT_REQUIRED` of `requireAlt`) are refused on every save, so a draft only holds them when the preset was tightened later. Publishing does not refuse them today, so Releases readiness does not either.

No routes, permissions, config keys or tables. Tests: `tests/ai-localization.test.mjs`, `tests/integration/i18n-releases.test.mjs`.

## Renderers, schema, types

- `magic-editor-x/render` (`shared/render`, bundled to `dist/render/index.{mjs,js}` by `scripts/build-server-bundle.mjs`, types `dist/render/index.d.ts`): `renderHtml(value, options)`, `renderTree`, `serializeNodes`, `renderText`, `renderMarkdown`, plus `escapeHtml`, `escapeMarkdown`, `inlineToHtml`, `inlineToText`, `DEFAULT_EMBED_HOSTS`, `enhanceCodeBlocks(root?)`, `copyText`. Options: `overrides[type](block, helpers)`, `links(ref) -> href|false|null` (checked with `sanitizeUrl`), `media(file) -> file` (re-validated), `rawHtml: 'allow'` + `sanitizeRaw`, `embedHosts`, `imageSizes`, `code: { lineNumbers?: boolean | 'block', copyButton?: boolean | { label, copiedLabel, failedLabel } }`, `focalPoint: 'data' | 'style'`, `blocks` (custom block SDK definitions). Inline HTML is re-parsed by `render/inline.mjs` `parseInline` (allow-list from the sanitize policy, entities decoded before URL checks, dangerous containers dropped with content) and turned into nodes by `inlineToNodes`. No dependencies, no Node built-ins, no framework imports (`tests/render-tree.test.mjs` checks the import graph, `verify:runtime` checks the bundles), deterministic.
- Render tree (`render/tree.mjs`): `createTreeBuilder(value, options, mode)` builds nodes `{ type: 'element', tag, attrs, children }` (lower-case names; attrs are strings or `true`), `{ type: 'text', value }` and `{ type: 'raw', html }`, plus internal `{ type: 'block', block, children }` wrappers that the React/Vue components use for `components`/slots; `renderTree` removes the wrappers. Blocks are separated by `\n` text nodes. A raw node only comes from `sanitizeRaw` (opt-in) and is always the only child of its element; adapters drop any other raw node. `renderHtml` = `serializeNodes(builder.nodes)` and is byte-identical to 2.2 (`tests/render.test.mjs`, `tests/render-tree.test.mjs`).
- **Adding a block type** (gallery, video, audio, table of contents, mention, ...): one entry in `RENDERERS` in `render/tree.mjs` returning `el(tag, attrs, children)` nodes (or null to omit) gives HTML, React and Vue output; add the matching entries in `render/text.mjs` and `render/markdown.mjs`, the policy/schema/types for the stored data, and a case in `tests/helpers/xss-corpus.mjs` `xssDocument`, so the React/Vue parity test covers it. Never build HTML strings in a renderer; boolean attributes are `true`, absent ones `undefined`/`false`. New attribute names that React spells differently go into `PROP_NAMES` (and `BOOLEAN_PROPS` for booleans) in `frameworks/react.mjs`.
- Overrides: return nodes (`helpers.h`, `helpers.textNode`, `helpers.inlineNodes`, `helpers.childNodes`), validated by `cleanOverrideNodes` (tag/attribute name patterns, no `on*`/`style`/`srcdoc`, denied tags such as script/style/object/form, URL attributes and `srcset` through `sanitizeUrl`, raw nodes dropped), or a string. A string is HTML: `renderHtml` writes it as it is (2.2 contract, the override escapes); in `renderTree` and the components it is used only with `rawHtml: 'allow'` + `sanitizeRaw`, as the raw child of `<div class="mex-override" data-mex-block="<type>">`, else the default output. `undefined`/`null`/numbers keep the default.
- Media (2.3): gallery `<figure class="mex-gallery mex-gallery-<layout> mex-gallery-cols-<n>" data-mex-layout data-mex-columns><ul class="mex-gallery-items"><li class="mex-gallery-item"><figure class="mex-gallery-figure"><img ...><figcaption>` + optional gallery `<figcaption>`; video `<figure class="mex-video"><video src controls preload="metadata" aria-label=<title> loop? playsinline muted? poster? width? height?><track kind src srclang label default?>…<a href=<file>>title</a></video><figcaption>`; audio the same with `<audio>` (no playsinline/muted/poster). Text: captions/alt (gallery), title + caption or the URL (video/audio); Markdown: one image per line (gallery), `[title](<url>)` + caption (video/audio). The `media(file)` hook runs for every file (gallery images, video/audio files, posters, tracks) and its result is re-validated for that kind.
- Focal point (image blocks, gallery images): default output `data-mex-focal-x`/`data-mex-focal-y` (0..1) on `<img>`, no inline style (CSP friendly: CSS cannot read the attributes into `object-position`, so a frontend that crops with `object-fit: cover` sets `img.style.objectPosition` from them in script, which the CSSOM allows under a strict `style-src`, or uses its framework's style binding). `focalPoint: 'style'` adds `style="object-position:X% Y%"`: the element node gets `style: { 'object-position': 'X% Y%' }` (`nodes.mjs` `safeStyle` allows only this property with percentage values; overrides cannot set it), React gets the `style` prop `{ objectPosition }`, Vue `{ 'object-position' }`. Media Library formats are resized, not cropped, so the same percentages hold for every `srcset` candidate.
- Code blocks: `language-<lang>` on `<code>` for codeFlask (language validated by the policy, `plaintext` fallback). `lineNumbers` adds `mex-code-lines` to `<pre>` and one `<span class="mex-code-line">` per line (newlines kept between spans, numbers from CSS counters, off above `MAX_NUMBERED_LINES` = 20000 lines); `'block'` follows codeFlask `showlinenumbers` like the editor does (on unless stored `false`; plain `code` blocks never). `copyButton` wraps the block in `<div class="mex-code-block" data-mex-code="copy">` with `<button type="button" class="mex-code-copy" data-mex-copy="code" data-mex-copied data-mex-failed>` and `<span class="mex-code-copy-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">`. Defaults off, so 2.2 output is unchanged. Markdown and text keep code as fenced (with language) or plain text.
- Table of contents and heading ids (`render/common.mjs` `annotateHeadings`, `shared/toc.mjs`): option `headingIds` (`true` every heading gets `id="mex-h-<blockId>"`, `false` never, default only when the value has a `toc` block). The anchor is the Editor.js block id, so it survives text edits, reordering and locales filled from another locale; invalid ids fall back to `mex-h-<n>` (n-th heading), repeats get `-2`, `-3`. A `toc` renders `<nav class="mex-toc mex-toc-<style>" aria-label="<title or options.toc.label or 'Table of contents'>">` with an optional `<p class="mex-toc-title">` and nested `<ol|ul class="mex-toc-list"><li class="mex-toc-item"><a href="#mex-h-…">text</a>…</li>` (headings of the whole document, toggle content included, within `minLevel..maxLevel`, empty ones skipped; plain text entries when ids are off); nothing when no heading matches. Text: title plus indented `1.`/`-` lines. Markdown: `**title**` and a nested list linking to GitHub-style slugs of the heading text (`#über-uns`, repeats `-1`), because Markdown pipelines (GitHub, markdown-it-anchor, rehype-slug) assign heading ids themselves; the Markdown output contains no HTML.
- Mentions: renderers add `class="mex-mention"` to `<a data-mex-mention>` (HTML, React, Vue; never stored, `storage: true` re-serialisation in resolve-references, find-replace and `resolveHrefs` keeps the markup as stored). The `links` resolver receives `mention: true` for them; `false` renders the stored text.
- `magic-editor-x/react` (`shared/frameworks/react.mjs`, `dist/react`, types `types/react.d.ts`): `MagicEditorXContent({ value, options, components })` (fragment, no hooks except in the copy block, which renders static markup when `React.useState` is missing as in React Server Components) and `treeToReact(nodes)`. `components[type]` receives `{ block, helpers: { text, url, inline, renderBlocks }, children }`. `createElement` only; `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` only for raw nodes. React 18 and 19 (peer `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`; React is the admin's peer, no extra install).
- `magic-editor-x/vue` (`shared/frameworks/vue.mjs`, `dist/vue`, types `types/vue.d.ts`): `MagicEditorXContent` (props `value`, `options`, `components`; scoped slots `block-<type>` with `{ block, helpers, children }` win over `components`, which get `block`/`helpers` props and the default output as default slot) and `treeToVue(nodes)`. `h()` only; `innerHTML` only for raw nodes; `true` attributes become ''. Vue is an optional peer (`^3.5.0`, `peerDependenciesMeta`) and a devDependency for tests.
- Both component bundles keep the framework external and bundle the renderer core. `tests/render-frameworks.test.mjs` renders the XSS corpus, fixtures and 1.x values through React `renderToStaticMarkup` and Vue `renderToString` and compares them with `renderHtml` after normalisation (htmlparser2: comments dropped, attributes sorted, entities decoded).
- `magic-editor-x/schema` (JSON Schema 2020-12, `$defs/data_<type>`), `magic-editor-x/types` (`MagicEditorXData`, `MagicEditorXBlock`, `BlockDataMap`, render types).
- `services/links.js` `resolveHrefs(value, { status })` re-renders internal-link hrefs from `links.urlPattern` and current slugs (server code, no permission checks). For permission-checked output use `services/references.js` `transform(items, { format, auth, status })` (see Content API and GraphQL output).

## Content API and GraphQL output (2.3)

Opt-in per request; without it responses are unchanged.

- REST: `?mex=html|text|markdown|json` on GET requests of Content API routes whose handler belongs to an `api::` content type (core `find`/`findOne` of collection and single types, and custom GET actions of the same controller). `middlewares/render-output.js` (registered with `strapi.server.use` in bootstrap) walks `ctx.body.data` along the schema (`utils/output-walk.js`: top-level fields, components, dynamic zones, populated relations; flat and `Strapi-Response-Format: v4` responses) and **replaces** every Magic Editor X value: `json` -> the stored document with resolved references (object or `null`), `html`/`text`/`markdown` -> the rendered string (`''` when empty). Raw HTML blocks are left out of rendered strings (renderer default). Admin routes (`route.info.type !== 'content-api'`), plugin routes and non-200 responses are never touched. Any other `mex` value (also repeated) -> 400 `ValidationError` `details: { key: 'mex', source: 'query', param: 'mex' }`, checked before the controller. An unexpected failure answers 500 with Strapi's generic body (never the stored values).
- `mex` is registered in `register.js` with `strapi.contentAPI.addQueryParams({ mex: { schema: z.enum([...]).optional(), matchRoute: GET routes with route.info.apiName } })` (Strapi's documented way to add Content API query params), so it passes with `api.rest.strictParams: true`. Strapi strips registered extra params before the Document Service. Strapi versions without `addQueryParams` accept `mex` only without strict params.
- Resolution (`services/references.js`, pure parts in `shared/resolve-references.mjs`), always with the caller's Content API auth (`ctx.state.auth`, GraphQL `context.state.auth`):
  - a target type is read only when `strapi.auth.verify(auth, { scope: ['<uid>.find'] })` passes (API tokens: full access, read-only, custom per action; users-permissions user or public role; same rule Strapi applies to populated relations); `api::` types only; Media Library files need `plugin::upload.content-api.find`;
  - Document Service `findMany({ filters: { documentId: { $in } }, locale, status })`, one query per type and locale (types without i18n: one per type), media one `db.query('plugin::upload.file')` query by id/documentId, custom-block definitions one query; `status` is `published` unless the REST request has `status=draft` (GraphQL: `draft` when the parent's `publishedAt` is `null`); every row passes `strapi.contentAPI.sanitize.output(row, model, { auth })` before any field is used;
  - bounds: 500 distinct references and 5 s per response (`LIMITS`); references over the limit or after the time budget stay unresolved; logs carry counts only.
- Results: internal link -> `href` from `links.urlPattern` with the sanitised slug (`renderLinkPattern`); unresolved (missing, draft-only, unreadable type, over the limit) -> the `<a>` is removed and only its text stays (no href, no reference attributes). A resolved mention also takes the entry's current title as its text (from the sanitised row: `title`, `name`, `label`, then the first text attribute); an unresolved mention keeps the text stored at insertion time, which is the title the author saw then (authored content, like any link text; it is never refreshed for callers who may not read the entry). Heading ids are on in `html` output whenever the value has a `toc` block. Embedded entry (custom block with `data.entry.documentId` and `data.contentType` `api::`) -> `data.entry = { ...displayFields, id, documentId, title, href }` from the sanitised live row (display fields: the custom block's `displayFields` plus the keys of the stored summary, scalar values only; title: `titleField`, then `title`, `name`, `label`, then the first text attribute), unresolved -> `data.entry = null` (the stored snapshot is dropped); rendered as `<div class="mex-block mex-entry mex-<type>" data-mex-block><a class="mex-entry-link" href>title</a></div>`, `[title](<href>)` or the title, nothing when unresolved. Image with `file.id`/`file.documentId` -> current `url`, `name`, `mime`, `ext`, `hash`, `width`, `height`, `size`, `formats`; `alt` only when the block has none; unresolved -> the stored file as stored. The same applies to every Media Library file slot (`shared/resolve-references.mjs` `mediaSlots`): gallery images and video posters like images, video/audio files and track files without `alt` and `formats`; all need `plugin::upload.content-api.find`. Internal links keep `data-mex-*` attributes in resolved output. Link titles are not added (the link text is authored content).
- GraphQL (`server/src/graphql.js`, registered in `register.js` through `strapi.plugin('graphql').service('extension').use(...)` only when the GraphQL plugin is installed): for every Magic Editor X attribute `x` of an `api::` content type or a component that is in the schema (`typeRegistry.has`), not private, output not disabled by `shadowCRUD(uid).field(x)`, and without an attribute named `xRendered`/`xResolved`: `xRendered(format: MagicEditorXFormat = HTML): String` (`HTML`, `TEXT`, `MARKDOWN`) and `xResolved: JSON`. Same resolution; values requested in one tick of a request are resolved in one batch per publication status. Component fields resolve against published versions and the default locale for links without a locale.
- `services/links.js` `resolveHrefs` is unchanged (server helper without permission checks).

## Paste, convert, migrate

- `shared/convert`: `htmlToBlocks(html, { parse, dataImages })` -> `{ blocks, report: { skipped, images } }` (pasted `<video>`/`<audio>` are skipped and reported as `unsupported-element`: media blocks hold Media Library files only; several pasted images become separate `image` blocks) on a minimal node interface (`dom-adapter.mjs` for DOMParser, `htmlparser-adapter.mjs` for htmlparser2), `markdownToBlocks(md, { parse? })` (marked lexer, GFM; raw HTML via htmlToBlocks or escaped), `strapiBlocksToEditor(value)`, `looksLikeMarkdown(text)`. Output uses only the editor's own tags; ids are deterministic (`cv<hash><index>`). marked and htmlparser2 are ESM-only and bundled into the server build.
- `admin/src/editor/paste.js` `createPasteHandler({ holder, editor, t, isAllowed, allowedHeadingLevels, uploadImageByUrl, uploadImageFile, canUpload, notify, onInserted })`: capture-phase paste on the holder; office HTML, 2+ block tags or Markdown text; never in code/raw/table cells/inputs; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V plain text; images via the upload routes (10 per paste, data: images max 5 MB, jpeg/png/gif/webp/avif), `file:`/`blob:` never fetched. Pure rules in `paste-logic.mjs`.
- `services/migrate.js` `run({ uid, from, to, format, locale, status, dryRun = true, overwrite, batchSize, limit })` (strict zod; `to` a top-level Magic Editor X field; `from` blocks/richtext/text/string/json; never writes `from`; skips a target with content unless `overwrite`) -> report `{ uid, from, to, format, dryRun, scanned, converted, skippedExisting, skippedEmpty, failed: [{ documentId, locale, code }], lossy: [{ documentId, locale, notes }] }`. `bin/magic-editor-x.mjs migrate` boots Strapi (`compileStrapi`, `createStrapi().load()`), routes Strapi's stdout to stderr, prints the report, exit 1 on failures.

## Authoring: @ mentions, code file names, pasted video and audio (2.4)

- `@` trigger (`admin/src/editor/mention-trigger.js`, pure rules in `mention-trigger-logic.mjs`): wherever the mention inline tool is offered (preset allows `hyperlink`, `linkTargets` `all`/`internal`, fetch client present), typing `@` at the start of a word in a `paragraph`, `header`, `list`, `checklist`, `quote`, `toggle` or `table` block opens entry suggestions at the caret. `findMentionQuery(textBeforeCaret)`: the `@` must be at the start of the block or follow white space or opening punctuation (`a@b`, e-mail addresses, `x.@` never trigger); the query is the text after it (max 50 characters, no leading space, no double space, no line break). The block is found by `.ce-block[data-id]` (`editor.blocks.getById`), so it stays right after collaborators' edits re-render a block. Never in code, raw HTML, inputs, links or chips (`a`), `data-mutation-free` views, read-only mode or during IME composition (`isComposing`, `compositionend` re-evaluates). Types from `/links/types` (cached, shared with the picker); none readable = no popup and the text stays. Each new `@` starts with the first readable type. Search `/links/search` debounced 200 ms; every newer query aborts the pending and the in-flight search (`AbortController` `signal` of the admin fetch client) and marks the listbox `aria-busy`; Enter while a search is pending inserts the first result when it arrives. Keys (window capture listener, runs before Editor.js, Markdown shortcuts and chip keys): ArrowDown/ArrowUp move, Enter or click inserts (Enter without results closes and keeps its normal job), Escape closes and keeps the typed text (that `@` does not reopen until a new `@` is typed), Tab moves to the content type select when there are several types (Tab/Enter/Escape there return to the text). ARIA: focus stays in the editable, which carries `aria-controls` (listbox), `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-activedescendant` and, when it has no role, `role="textbox"` + `aria-multiline` while open (restored on close); polite live region with the result count. Picking calls `tools/mention.js` `insertMentionChip(range, item, labels)` (also used by the toolbar tool) on the `@query` range: same chip and attributes as the tool, change reported by an `input` event (Editor.js onChange -> form value, collaboration). The popup (`.mex-mention-popup`, fixed, `zIndices.popover`, follows the caret on scroll and resize) is a sibling of the holder, so it stays inside the fullscreen dialog; the active option is kept visible by scrolling the list only (`scrollIntoView` would scroll the page behind a fixed popup).
- Code block file name: `codeFlask` data gains optional `filename` (`cleanCodeFilename`: tabs/newlines to spaces, C0/C1 controls, DEL, bidi and zero-width marks removed, white space collapsed, trimmed, max 200 code points `MAX_CODE_FILENAME`; omitted when empty, so stored data without it is unchanged). A plain-text label, never interpreted as a path. Schema `data_codeFlask.filename` (string 1-200), `CodeFlaskData.filename?`. The plain `code` block has no file name (its policy drops the key). Editor: input above the code (`.mex-code__filename`, keys kept from Editor.js, Enter moves into the code), text when read-only. Renderers, only with a file name: HTML/React/Vue `<figure class="mex-code-figure"><figcaption class="mex-code-filename">name</figcaption>` + the unchanged `<pre>` or copy-button wrapper; text: the name on its own line before the code; Markdown: ` ```js title="name" ` (language always written, `plaintext` when none; `"` and `\` backslash-escaped; a name with a backtick uses a `~~~` fence). Import: `parseFenceInfo(info)` reads `title=`/`filename=` (double quotes to the last quote, single quotes or bare) and the language (first word unless it is an attribute); a file name without a valid language gives `codeFlask` with `plaintext`; HTML `<figure>` with `<figcaption>` and one `<pre>` (the renderers' output) is imported with the caption as file name. Output for blocks without a file name is byte-identical.
- Pasted video and audio: `htmlToBlocks(html, { media: 'collect' })` turns `<video>`/`<audio>` (block level, inline or in a `<figure>` whose `<figcaption>` becomes the caption) with an http(s) `src` (else the first `<source src>` of the matching type) into placeholder blocks listed in `report.media: [{ index, kind, src, title, caption, loop, muted?, poster?, tracks: [{ src, kind, srclang, label, default }] (max 8) }]`; `data:`, `blob:`, `file:` and relative sources give `{ index: -1, kind, src: '' }` and skip reason `media`. Without the option the 2.3 behaviour stays (`unsupported-element`). The paste handler collects only when the admin can upload, the field allows `video` or `audio` and `uploadMediaByUrl` exists (`decidePaste({ media })` then converts a lone `<video>`/`<audio>`); a kind the preset does not allow counts as dropped. At most `MAX_REMOTE_MEDIA` = 3 per paste; for each: file via `POST /media/byUrl`, poster via `POST /image/byUrl`, tracks via `POST /media/byUrl` `kind: 'track'` (a poster or track that fails is left out), block data from `mediaBlockData` through `prepareEditorValue`, inserted where the element was. Failed or blocked files: one warning `editor.paste.mediaFailed` with the count (the URL helpers show no notification of their own).
- Server `services/editor.js` `uploadMediaUrl(url, kind, user)`: http(s) only (`validateHttpUrl`), `fetchBounded` with the kind's MIME list (`MEDIA_TYPES`: video `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime`, `video/webm`, `video/ogg`; audio `audio/mpeg`, `audio/mp3`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/x-m4a`, `audio/aac`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`, `audio/wave`, `audio/webm`, `audio/flac`, `audio/x-flac`; track `text/vtt`), size cap `uploads.maxMediaBytes` (tracks 512 KiB), 60 s per hop, 2 redirects (each re-checked), then the file signature must match the declared type (`detectMediaContainer`: ftyp/EBML/OggS/fLaC/RIFF WAVE/ID3 or MPEG frame/ADTS; `isWebVtt`: UTF-8, no NUL, `WEBVTT` header), else 415. Stored through the upload service with the admin as creator, canonical MIME and extension, name from the URL path (`safeFilename`). At most 3 media downloads at once per process (429), because the body is buffered in memory. `uploads.allowPrivateOrigins` (exact `URL.origin`s) lets the image and media by-URL routes fetch those private or loopback origins, never following their redirects (intranet media servers, test hosts); every other private, loopback, link-local or reserved address stays refused, also after DNS resolution and redirects.

| Method | Path           | Actions        | Handler                 | Input                                                          | Output                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------ | -------------- | -------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/media/byUrl` | access, upload | `editor.uploadMediaUrl` | `{ url (max 2048), kind: 'video'\|'audio'\|'track' }` (strict) | `{ success: 1, file: { url, id, documentId, name, mime, ext, hash, size } }`; `{ success: 0, message }` 400 (URL, kind, private host), 413, 415 (type or signature), 429, 502, 504 |

| Config                        | Default | Bounds                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| `uploads.maxMediaBytes`       | 50 MiB  | 1 byte to 200 MiB            |
| `uploads.allowPrivateOrigins` | `[]`    | max 20 exact http(s) origins |

No new permission actions; `upload` = `plugin::upload.assets.create`.

## AI extras and grammar check (2.3)

- Rules: nothing is sent unless the owner turned the feature on in Settings (`ai.enabled` + `ai.allowImages` for alt text, `ai.enabled` + `ai.allowFieldActions` for whole-field actions, `languageTool.enabled` for grammar); every AI route answers 403 for fields with `disableAi` (the grammar check is not AI and ignores it; it answers 403 for fields with `disableGrammar`). Results are suggestions: the server never writes content. Logs carry the action and error code only.
- Alt text (`services/ai.js` `altText`, `utils/media-image.js`): the file is loaded with the upload service and checked like the upload plugin's `findOne` (`createPermissionsManager({ action: 'plugin::upload.read', model: 'plugin::upload.file' })`, creator with roles populated); private providers get `signFileUrls`. The largest stored variant (original or `formats.*`) with a long edge up to 1568 px and at most 3.5 MB is sent; local files are read only from `<public>/uploads` (real path inside it), remote URLs only through `fetchBounded` (public hosts, 2 redirects, image MIME types, size cap). The media type comes from the file signature (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP; else 415). Anthropic: `{ type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type, data } }` before the text; OpenAI and compatible: `{ type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: 'data:<mime>;base64,...' } }`. Language from `locale` (`Intl.DisplayNames`, default English). Answer: plain text, controls removed, cut at a word boundary at 150 characters. Counter `ai:<adminId>`.
- Whole-field actions (`shared/ai-fields.mjs`): `collectSegments(data)` lists the inline HTML strings (`searchableFields` of find and replace, html kind) as `{ blockId, path, html }`; only these are sent. Total plain text over `ai.maxInputChars` is 413. `translate` sends chunks of `{ segments: [{ id, html }] }` (chunk text at most `min(maxInputChars, maxOutputTokens * 1.5)`, max 20 chunks, one counter hit per chunk) and expects the same JSON back; the answer must contain every id once (else 502 `BAD_RESPONSE`), each string is sanitised (`sanitizeInlineHtml`) and links whose `href` the original did not contain are unwrapped (`restrictLinks`). The admin checks the ids again, sanitises (DOMPurify), shows a preview, verifies the field still holds the sent strings and replaces with `applySegments` (ids, types, tunes and all other data unchanged; one undo step). `summarize` returns plain text (copy or insert as a paragraph).
- Grammar (`services/grammar.js`): `POST {baseUrl}/v2/check` form-urlencoded `text`, `language` (`languageToolLanguage(locale)`: region kept, `en`->`en-US`, `de`->`de-DE`, `pt`->`pt-PT`, none -> `auto`), `level=picky` when set, `username` + `apiKey` when stored. Plain text per string (`segmentText`: text nodes, `<br>` = newline) joined with blank lines into requests of at most 20,000 characters (max 5 per check, 60,000 in total, 413 above); matches crossing a separator are dropped, the rest mapped back (`locateInJoined`), max 500. Counter `grammar:<adminId>` (`languageTool.requestsPerMinute`). The admin (`GrammarPanel`) highlights with CSS Custom Highlight `mex-grammar` and applies a replacement with `replaceInSegment` only when the range lies inside one text node and still holds the flagged text.
- Admin helper for other image tools (`admin/src/editor/ai-alt-text.js`): `createAltTextSuggester({ post, getTarget, getLocale })` -> `suggest(fileId, { signal })`, `createAltSuggestion({ t, getFileId, suggest, onUse, readOnly })` -> `{ element, refresh, destroy }`, `mediaFileId(file)`, `altTextErrorText(t, info)`. `buildTools` passes `ctx.suggestAltText` (only when allowed) as `config.suggestAltText` of the image tool.

## Block-aware AI and private image storage (2.4)

Block actions (`shared/ai-blocks.mjs`, `services/ai.js` `blockAction`, `controllers/ai.js` `blocks`, admin `BlockAiDialog.jsx`):

| Method | Path                 | Handler     | Policies                                                                                                                   | Body / answer                                                                                                                                              |
| ------ | -------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/ai/blocks/:action` | `ai.blocks` | `admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` + `admin::hasPermissions` [`plugin::magic-editor-x.access`, `plugin::magic-editor-x.ai.use`] | `{ target: { uid, field }, segments: [{ blockId, path, html }] (1-200, each block path once), language?, tone? }` (strict zod) -> `{ data: { segments } }` |

- `:action` is `improve` (rewrite), `shorten`, `translate` (`language` from `config.ai.languages`) or `tone` (`tone` from `config.ai.tones`); anything else 404 before a provider call. Errors: unknown field 404, `disableAi` 403, `ai.enabled` off 503 `DISABLED`, plain text over `maxInputChars` 413, rate limit 429 (one `ai:<adminId>` hit per provider call), provider errors as for the other AI routes (`AIProviderError` with `details.code`).
- Permissions: `ai.use` plus the owner's `ai.enabled`. Block actions are selection-scoped like the text actions (the admin picks the blocks, the same `maxInputChars` bound applies), so they do **not** need `ai.allowFieldActions`, which gates sending a whole field at once. No new RBAC action.
- Protocol: the JSON segment protocol of the whole-field translation (`runSegments`): chunks by the output budget (at most 20 calls), ids `"0".."n"`; the answer must name every id exactly once (canonical decimal), every value a string of at most `min(20000, 4 x input + 400)` characters with some text left, otherwise 502 `BAD_RESPONSE`. Each string is sanitised with the field preset's inline tags (`allowedInlineTags` -> `inlineSanitizerFor`, all inline tags for presets without an inline list) and `restrictLinks` unwraps every link the sent string did not hold. Only the sent strings travel; block ids, types, tunes, URLs and other data stay in the browser. Content is never logged (`blocks-<action>` and the code only).
- Admin: entry points are the block selection bar (two or more selected blocks, button "AI for the chosen blocks"), the block menu of every text block (Editor.js block tune `aiBlockTune`, only when AI is allowed for the field; it has no `save()`, so nothing is stored), and the keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G without selected text opens it for the selected blocks or the block with the caret (with selected text the inline AI tool runs, as before). The selection bar stays while focus is inside it and keeps Tab inside the bar (Editor.js handles Tab on `document` in the capture phase while a block is current), so Escape, then Shift+Tab reaches it. The dialog shows a word diff (old text above new text when less than half of it stays, `changeViews`) (`diffText` + `TextOps` from `VersionDiff.jsx`), and "Apply to blocks" runs `applyBlockResult(data, sent, result, preset)`: the result must name exactly the sent strings (`MISMATCH`), the document must still hold every sent string unchanged (`CHANGED` -> "These blocks changed ..."), then `applySegments` writes them and only the changed blocks are fixed with `fixPresetViolations`; the content is applied through `replaceContent` (one undo step, pushed to the collaboration room). Hidden when the field has `disableAi`, the admin lacks `ai.use`, AI is off or the field is read-only (read-only users, live room without edit rights).
- Selection action (`POST /ai/:action`, unchanged route and body): since 2.4 the suggestion is sanitised with the field preset's inline tags and links the selection did not hold are unwrapped; the dialog shows it as a word diff and the suggestion is inserted outside the inline elements whose edge the selection ended on (`editor/ai-selection.js`), so formatting that the selection crossed is kept and not nested.

Private image storage for alt text (`ai.altText.allowPrivateOrigins`, config only):

- Default `[]`: `utils/media-image.js` fetches remote image URLs from public addresses only. Each entry must be an exact `URL.origin` (`http://minio.internal:9000`), at most 20; the validator refuses link-local, unspecified and cloud metadata hosts (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`, `169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`, `metadata.google.internal`) at boot (`isListablePrivateOrigin`).
- `utils/url-security.js` `privateOriginOptions(url, origins)` (shared with `qualityChecks.externalLinks.allowPrivateOrigins`) returns fetch options only when the URL's origin is listed exactly (another port, scheme or host name of the same machine is not): private and loopback addresses are allowed, the host is resolved once and the socket is pinned to that address (DNS rebinding), redirects are never followed (`requestWithoutRedirect`; a 3xx fails with `IMAGE_UNREADABLE`, also to the same origin), and addresses in the refused ranges above stay refused also when a listed host name resolves to them. Size (3.5 MB), type (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP by signature) and edge (1568 px) caps are unchanged. Signed URLs keep their query; URLs are never logged.
- Settings > Configuration shows the list read-only (`GET /settings` -> `environment.altTextPrivateOrigins`).

## Editor field extras

- Markdown shortcuts (`editor/markdown-shortcuts*.{js,mjs}`), find and replace (`shared/find-replace.mjs` + `FindReplacePanel`, CSS Custom Highlight `mex-find`), shortcuts dialog (Ctrl/Cmd+/), focus mode, `BlockSelectionBar` (Editor.js `.ce-block--selected`), quality panel (`QualityPanel`, `useQualityIssues`) with preset violations, `lang`/`dir` from the content locale. The image tool is `MexImageTool` (`tools/alt-text.js`, subclass of `@editorjs/image` adding alt text, the decorative flag and the focal point control). Media tools (`tools/media.js`: `GalleryTool`, `VideoTool`, `AudioTool`; pure logic in `tools/media-logic.mjs`; focal point control `tools/focal-point.js`: disclosure button, click/tap on the preview, arrow keys 1 % / Shift 10 %, reset, polite live value) open the Strapi Media Library dialog through `openMediaLibrary({ multiple, allowedTypes: ['images'|'videos'|'audios'|'files'], accept(asset), onSelect(assets) })`; `EditorField` filters the picked assets with `accept` and returns focus to the trigger. They are offered only with `plugin::upload.read` (`config.permissions.mediaLibrary`, tool config `canBrowse`); without it they are hidden from the toolbox and existing blocks explain why no files can be chosen. Gallery: add (multiple), move earlier/later, remove, per-image alt (default: the file's Media Library alternative text; `requireAlt`/decorative as in the image block), caption, focal point, layout and columns. Video/audio: choose/replace, title, caption, loop (+ muted and poster for video), WebVTT tracks (kind, language defaulting to the content locale, label, one default).
- Field readiness and edits (`editor/input-tracking.mjs`): the field reports content to the form only after the person edited it (Editor.js also reports its normalisation of stored content on the first render). User input (`pointerdown`, `keydown`, `input`, `paste`, `drop`, capture phase on the holder) is tracked from before Editor.js renders, and edits made while Editor.js was starting are saved on `onReady`; after the Content Manager's create -> edit redirect several fields mount at once and text typed before the field's own effects ran used to stay out of the form (Save stayed disabled). The holder (`[data-testid="magic-editor-x"]`) carries `aria-busy="true"` while loading and `data-mex-ready="true"` once Editor.js is ready and every listener is attached; browser tests wait for `data-mex-ready` instead of sleeping.
- Editor styles (`editor/tools/styles.js`) are one global style rendered by the first mounted field only (`editor/style-owners.mjs`, `SharedEditorStyles`); one copy per field made styled-components rebuild every copy on each mount and unmount (seconds of blocked main thread on pages with several fields).
- `apply-remote.js`: default tune values count as "no tune" in `blockKey` (`shared/default-tunes.mjs`); more than 150 changed blocks (and a quarter of the document) are applied with one `render` instead of per-block updates (Editor.js notifies every block on each mutation).

## Block comments (2.3)

- Content type `plugin::magic-editor-x.comment` (table `magic_editor_comments`, hidden from the Content Manager and the Content-Type Builder, no Content API route): `contentType`, `entryId`, `entryLocale` (null for types without i18n), `fieldName` (the field identity of the version / room key `uid|documentId|locale|field` as columns; 2.4: `<path without indices>#<fieldKey>` inside repeatable components and dynamic zones), `blockId` (Editor.js block id, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`), `threadId` (documentId of the root; null on the root), `excerpt` (root only, plain one-line text, max 200), `body` (plain text, max 4000 after `normalizeCommentBody`: CRLF to LF, tabs to spaces, C0/C1 controls, bidi overrides and zero-width marks removed, at most two blank lines), `authorId` (admin id) + `authorName` (name snapshot), `editedAt`, `resolved`, `resolvedAt`, `resolvedById` + `resolvedByName`. Access through `services/comments.js` (query engine).
- API shapes: thread `{ id, blockId, excerpt, status: 'open'|'resolved', resolvedAt, resolvedBy: { name }|null, createdAt, updatedAt (latest activity), comments: [comment] }`; comment `{ id, threadId, body, author: { name|null, own, deleted }, createdAt, updatedAt, editedAt }`. Admin ids are never returned; `own` tells the caller whether they wrote it. Comments are never part of the field value, version history or Content API output.
- Rules: every route needs `access` + `comments.read` and Content Manager read on the document, locale and field (`services/access.js` `checkField`, 404 otherwise; a comment id of another document answers 404 too). Commenting, replying, resolving and reopening need `comments.write` but no update right (reviewers). Editing: author only. Deleting: own comment with `comments.write`; anyone's, or a thread with replies by other people, with `comments.moderate`. Limits: `comments.perMinute` new comments per admin (counter `comments:<adminId>` in `magic_editor_x_counters`, 429), 1000 comments per field and locale, 200 replies per thread (400 `TOO_MANY_COMMENTS`). Handlers log nothing.
- Retention (`utils/comment-retention.js`): a Document Service middleware deletes the comments of every document locale a `delete` removed (`result.entries[].locale`), after the delete; an `admin::user` `afterDelete` lifecycle clears `authorId`/`authorName` and `resolvedById`/`resolvedByName` of the deleted admin (the text stays, shown as "Deleted user"). Rows written around the Document Service (raw SQL, `db.query`) are not cleaned up.
- Admin: toolbar toggle with the open-thread count, `CommentsPanel` (pattern of the quality panel: new thread on a chosen block, open threads first, detached threads (block no longer in the document) still readable and resolvable, "Show resolved threads", reply, resolve/reopen, edit/delete own with ConfirmDialog, live region) and `CommentMarkers` (button with the open-thread count at the inline end of each block, rendered next to the Editor.js holder, never inside it). `useComments` polls `GET /comments` every 15 s while the field is on screen and the tab visible (8 s with the panel open), on window focus and after every own action; the database is the source of truth, so it works across processes. Config `comments.enabled: false` hides the UI and the routes answer 404.

## Audit trail, synced source versions and the link check "Run now" (2.4)

Routes (prefix `/magic-editor-x`, all with `admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` + `admin::hasPermissions`):

| Method | Path                                         | Actions                         | Handler                    | Input                                                                                                                                                                     | Output                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/audit`                                     | audit.read (+ see access rules) | `audit.list`               | `?uid&documentId&locale&field&fieldKey&actor&event&from&to&page&pageSize` (strict; `pageSize` 1-100, default 25; `page` 1-10000; `from`/`to` ISO dates; `actor` admin id) | `{ data: [event], meta: { scope: 'field'\|'global', enabled, pagination: { page, pageSize, pageCount, total } } }`, newest first                                                                                 |
| GET    | `/audit/actors`                              | audit.read, settings.read       | `audit.actors`             |                                                                                                                                                                           | `{ data: [{ id, name }] }` (admins in the trail, max 200)                                                                                                                                                        |
| GET    | `/templates/:id/versions`                    | access, templates.manage        | `templates.versions`       |                                                                                                                                                                           | `{ data: [{ id, version, trigger: 'manual'\|'restore', label, name, createdAt, createdBy: { name }\|null, blockCount }] }`, newest first; 404 unless `:id` is a synced source                                    |
| GET    | `/templates/:id/versions/:versionId`         | access, templates.manage        | `templates.version`        |                                                                                                                                                                           | `{ data: { ...version, content } }` (`content`: the stored Editor.js document); 404 for a version of another source                                                                                              |
| PUT    | `/templates/:id/versions/:versionId`         | access, templates.manage        | `templates.renameVersion`  | `{ label }` (max 120, no control characters, `''`/`null` clears; strict)                                                                                                  | `{ data: version }`                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| POST   | `/templates/:id/versions/:versionId/restore` | access, templates.manage        | `templates.restoreVersion` | empty body                                                                                                                                                                | `{ data: template }`: a normal update (strict schema, sanitising, scope check) with the version's blocks and name; description, scope, enabled and order stay; a new version with `trigger: 'restore'` is stored |

Permission: `plugin::magic-editor-x.audit.read` (uid `audit.read` in `registerMany`, "Read the audit trail"). `GET /config` adds `data.audit: { enabled }` and `permissions.auditRead`.

Audit trail:

- What is recorded (never content, e-mail addresses, IP addresses or tokens): `event`, target `{ uid, documentId, locale, field }`, `counts` (non-negative integers, at most 12 keys), `blockIds` (at most 20 Editor.js ids), `meta` (at most 8 keys of identifier-like strings `/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,64}$/` or lists of them), actor, time. `shared/audit.mjs` `cleanAuditInput` enforces the shape for every caller. Events: `entry.create|update|publish|unpublish|discard|delete` (per changed editor field, counts `{ added, removed, changed, moved, blocks }`), `version.create|restore|rename` (`counts.version`), `ai.action` (`meta.action`, `counts.segments` or `counts.images`), `comment.create|reply|resolve|reopen|delete|moderate` (`meta.threadId`, the block id), `template.create|update|delete` and `synced.create|update|delete|restore` (`counts.blocks`, `meta.kind`), `settings.update` (`meta.keys`: the submitted top-level keys, never values), `linkcheck.run` (`counts.documents|checked|problems|pruned`, `meta.trigger`, `meta.complete`). Other features may add `<area>.<verb>` events.
- Service for other features: `strapi.plugin('magic-editor-x').service('audit').record({ event, target?: { uid?, documentId?, locale?, field? }, counts?, blockIds?, meta?, actor? }) -> Promise<boolean>` (never throws; `recordMany([...])` for several). `actor`: omitted = the admin of the current request (`strapi.requestContext`, admin routes only), `'system'`, or an admin user object / `{ id, name }`. Content API writes are recorded with `actor.kind: 'api'` and no id. Server code can use `utils/audit-record.js` `recordAudit(strapi, input)`, which also tolerates a missing service.
- Field identity: `shared/audit.mjs` `fieldIdentity(path, value)` is the one place that decides it (2.4 field identity contract): the path for top-level and single-component fields, `<path without indices>#<fieldKey>` for positional fields whose value has a `fieldKey`, else the positional path. `GET /audit` accepts `fieldKey` next to `field`.
- Field changes: `utils/audit-trail.js` registers a Document Service middleware for `api::` types with editor fields. It reads the editor fields (only them: `guardQuery` fields + populate) of the affected versions before and after `create`, `update`, `publish`, `unpublish`, `discardDraft` and `delete` (draft for Draft & Publish writes, published for publish/unpublish and types without Draft & Publish, every locale the call touches) and records one event per changed field. `fieldChanges(before, after)` compares blocks by id and a JSON fingerprint (no word diff): linear, about 6 ms for 5000 blocks (`npm run bench` operation `auditChanges`). Writes around the Document Service are not recorded. A failure is logged without data and never blocks the write.
- Storage: table `magic_editor_x_audit (id bigint, created_at ms, event, uid, document_id, locale, field, actor_id, actor_name, actor_kind 'admin'|'api'|'system'|'deleted', counts JSON, block_ids JSON, meta JSON)` created in `services/store.js`, indexes `(uid, document_id, locale, id)`, `(created_at)`, `(actor_id, id)`. A table instead of a content type: append-only, high volume, no documentId, publication or Content Manager needed (like the link check tables). Inserts go through `strapi.db.transaction`, which joins the caller's transaction (no second SQLite connection, rolled back with it).
- Config: `audit.enabled` (default `true`: the trail holds no content and answers "who changed this" for editors and owners; `false` stops recording and the middleware's reads), `audit.retentionDays` (default 180, 0 keeps everything, max 3660). Pruning: once an hour one process (one-time key `audit:prune:<hour>` in `magic_editor_x_locks`) deletes older rows in batches of 1000 (at most 50 per run). A deleted admin user's rows keep the event and lose `actor_id`/`actor_name` (`actor_kind: 'deleted'`, shown as "Deleted user"; `admin::user` `afterDelete` lifecycle).
- Access (decided): with `field` (+ `uid`, `documentId`) the listing is field-scoped and needs `audit.read` plus Content Manager read on the document, locale and field (`services/access.js` `checkField`, 404 otherwise); actors carry `{ kind, name, own, deleted }` without ids. Without `field` (global, also filtered by type or document) it needs `audit.read` + `settings.read` (403 otherwise), because it spans documents; actors also carry `id` (for the actor filter). Records hold no content, so a global reader learns which documents and fields changed, by whom and how many blocks, not what.
- Strapi Enterprise Audit Logs: when `strapi.has('audit-logs-lifecycle')` (Enterprise license with the feature, as `@strapi/review-workflows` checks it), bootstrap registers every event as `magic-editor-x.<event>` with `registerEvent(name, transform)` (`resource: { type: 'magic-editor-x', uid, id: documentId }`, `details: { locale, field, counts, blockIds, meta }`; other events on first use) and `record` emits it on `strapi.eventHub`; Strapi stores it only for admin requests and with its own actor data. Without the feature nothing is emitted; webhooks never fire for these names.
- Admin: Settings > Magic Editor X > Audit trail (`pages/AuditPage`, link permission `audit.read`; the page needs `settings.read` too): filters (event, actor, content type uid, document id, date range) and page in the URL, DS `Table` from the `large` breakpoint, a card list below, admin `Pagination`, empty/loading/error states, "Recording is off" when disabled. The version history modal gets "Versions" / "Activity" tabs for admins with `audit.read` (`FieldActivity`, `GET /audit?uid&documentId&locale&field`, 20 per page, "Show older activity"). Restoring a field version calls `GET /history/:id?intent=restore`, which records `version.restore` when the caller may update the document.

Synced source versions:

- Rows of `plugin::magic-editor-x.document-snapshot` with `contentType: 'plugin::magic-editor-x.template'`, `entryId: <source documentId>`, `entryLocale: null`, `fieldName: 'blocks'`, `roomId` `plugin::magic-editor-x.template|<id>|-|blocks`, plus the 2.4 columns `sourceName` (the name at that version), `authorId` and `authorName` (name snapshot; the id is never returned; both cleared when the admin is deleted). Chosen over a new table because numbering under the lease `snapver:<roomId>`, the content hash, labels and pruning are the field-version mechanics; `GET /history/:id` never serves them (`checkField` answers 404 for non-`api::` types).
- `services/synced-versions.js`: every create/update of a `kind: 'synced'` row through `services/templates.js` (also duplicate and restore) stores a version unless name and blocks equal the latest version; at most `history.maxSnapshotsPerField` per source (oldest removed). Deleting a source deletes its versions. Templates and patterns get none (404 on the version routes).
- Admin: Settings > Templates, edit view of a synced source: "Versions" section (`pages/TemplatesPage/SyncedVersions.jsx`): list, preview, "Changes" against the content in the form (`VersionDiff`, `shared/diff.mjs`), rename, restore with ConfirmDialog (says when unsaved form changes are lost; afterwards the view reloads the saved source, so the Blocker sees no change).

Scheduled link check:

- `qualityChecks.externalLinks.schedule.tz` (optional IANA name, no default = server time zone) is validated at boot with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (`utils/time-zone.js`; `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` has no `UTC` in V8) and passed as `strapi.cron.add({ name: { task, options: { rule, tz } } })`; Strapi 5.61 hands `tz` to croner 10 as `timezone`. The one-time key `linkrun:<minute>` uses the fire time's minute since the epoch (an absolute instant), so it is the same on every process whatever the zone.
- `GET /quality/link-schedule` adds `tz` and `nextRunAt` (the job's `nextInvocation()`), and `running` is true while any process holds the `links:schedule` lease; Settings `environment.linkSchedule` adds `tz`, `nextRunAt`, `running`. `runNow(actor)` records `linkcheck.run` with the admin as actor.
- Settings > Configuration: "Scheduled link check" section (`LinkScheduleSection`): state, schedule with time zone and next run, last run; "Run now" for admins with `settings.update` (hidden with an explanation otherwise); while running it polls `GET /quality/link-schedule` every 3 s (at most 300 times) and announces the end in a polite live region; 409 `RUNNING` and 400 `DISABLED` are shown inline.

## Templates, block patterns and the in-field preview (2.3)

- Content type `plugin::magic-editor-x.template` (table `magic_editor_templates`, hidden from the Content Manager and the Content-Type Builder, no Content API route): `name` (max 100), `description`, `kind` (`template` = whole starting content \| `pattern` = insertable block sequence), `blocks` (Editor.js document), `scope` (`{ all, presets: [preset name], fields: [{ uid, field }] }`, field paths without indices such as `sections.body`), `enabled`, `sortOrder`, `createdByName` (display name snapshot; no admin id is stored), timestamps. Access through `services/templates.js` (query engine).
- API shape: `{ id, name, description, kind, blocks, blockCount, scope, enabled, sortOrder, createdBy: { name } | null, createdAt, updatedAt }`.
- Writes: strict zod schema, then `cleanEditorValue(blocks, { rawHtml })` with `rawHtml` `sanitize` (or `disable` when the plugin disables raw HTML; templates never keep unsanitised raw HTML), at least 1 and at most 200 blocks, 256 KiB of JSON, at most 500 templates; scope fields must be Magic Editor X fields of `api::` types. Handlers log nothing.
- Scope (`shared/templates.mjs` `templateMatchesTarget`): `all`, or the field's preset name (`resolveFieldPreset(options).name`) is in `presets`, or `{ uid, field without indices }` is in `fields`. The editor list requires `access` and Content Manager read on the content type (404 otherwise).
- Insertion (admin, `prepareInsertion` + `insertBlocksAt`): blocks whose type the field preset does not allow are left out, heading levels and links are fixed like "Fix automatically" (`fixPresetViolations`), `maxBlocks` truncates, every block gets a fresh 10-character id; a template replaces the field content (confirmation when the field is not empty), a pattern goes after the block the user worked on last (or replaces an empty field). The new document goes through `replaceContent` (Editor.js block API, the shared Yjs document, undo). Managers save the selection (block selection bar) or the whole field (insert dialog) as a new template (`POST /templates`).
- Settings > Magic Editor X > Templates (`pages/TemplatesPage`, link permission `templates.manage`): list (enable, preview, edit, duplicate, reorder, delete with ConfirmDialog), create/edit view with an embedded editor (`EditorFieldBody` with an empty target: no collaboration, history, comments or template insertion) and the Blocker.
- Preview (`FieldPreview`, `components/RenderedContent`): toolbar toggle and Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+P; renders `currentData` with `MagicEditorXContent` from `shared/frameworks/react.mjs` (code line numbers on); raw HTML only when the plugin keeps raw HTML and the preset allows `raw`, then sanitised again with a strict DOMPurify profile; embeds become a labelled link placeholder (no iframe); tables get their own scroll region; clicks on links are prevented. The editor stays mounted (hidden) while the preview is shown; works for read-only users.

## Range comments, @mentions and notifications (2.4)

Extends "Block comments (2.3)"; block comments, their routes and stored rows are unchanged (a thread without `anchor` is a block comment).

Routes (prefix `/magic-editor-x`, all with `admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` + `admin::hasPermissions`; comments off (`comments.enabled: false`) answers 404):

| Method | Path                        | Actions                               | Handler                 | Input                                                                                   | Output                                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/comments/mentionable`     | access, comments.read, comments.write | `comments.mentionable`  | `?uid&documentId&locale&field&fieldKey?&q?` (strict; `q` max 50, no control characters) | `{ data: [{ id, name }] }` (max 8; `id` = the admin user's documentId; never e-mail addresses); 404 not readable, 409 `FIELD_KEY_REQUIRED`, 429 |
| GET    | `/notifications`            | access, comments.read                 | `notifications.list`    | `?page&pageSize&unread` (strict; page 1-20, pageSize 1-50, default 10; `unread=true`)   | `{ data: [notification], meta: { unread, pagination: { page, pageSize, total, pageCount } } }`, newest first                                    |
| POST   | `/notifications/read-all`   | access, comments.read                 | `notifications.readAll` | `{ threadIds? }` (max 100 documentIds; without: all)                                    | `{ data: { updated } }`                                                                                                                         |
| POST   | `/notifications/:id/read`   | access, comments.read                 | `notifications.read`    |                                                                                         | `{ data: { id, read: true } }`; 404 for someone else's                                                                                          |
| POST   | `/notifications/:id/unread` | access, comments.read                 | `notifications.unread`  |                                                                                         | `{ data: { id, read: false } }`; 404 for someone else's                                                                                         |

Changed routes (additive): `POST /comments` accepts `anchor` (below) and `mentions` (max 20 opaque ids from `mentionable`); `POST /comments/:id/replies` and `PUT /comments/:id` accept `mentions` (`PUT` without `mentions` keeps the list). Their responses add `meta.droppedMentions` (mentions the server left out). `GET /comments` threads add `anchor` (or null), comments add `mentions: [{ id, name, you }]`, `meta.notifications: [{ id, threadId, commentId, kind }]` (the caller's unread ones on this field). A reply marks the replier's own notifications of that thread read. No new permission.

Range anchors (`shared/comment-anchor.mjs`, `shared/comment-relpos.mjs`, `admin/src/editor/comment-anchor-dom.js`):

- Stored in the root row's `anchor` JSON column (null for block comments and rows before 2.4): `{ path, start, end, quote: { exact, prefix, suffix } }`. `path`: data key path of the text field in the block (`text`, `caption`, `items.1.content`, `content.0.2`; `ANCHOR_PATH_PATTERN`, at most 8 keys, no `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype`) or null. `start`/`end`: base64 of an encoded Yjs `RelativePosition` (at most 512 bytes; both or none; only with a path) on that field's Y.Text in the live room, `start` with assoc 0 (first character of the range), `end` with assoc -1 (last character), so text typed at the edges does not join the range. `quote.exact` max 500 characters, `prefix`/`suffix` max 32, control characters except line feeds removed (`cleanAnchor`). The server validates the shape (strict zod) and never decodes the positions; the block id stays in `blockId`.
- Text model: a Y.Text holds the field's HTML source. `htmlTextMap(html)` gives the text a reader sees (tags dropped, `<br>` as a line feed, comments dropped, `&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot; &apos; &nbsp;`, numeric and a small set of named references decoded; a `<` not followed by a letter, `/`, `!` or `?` is text) with the source range of every UTF-16 unit; the admin builds the DOM text of the field element with the same rules (`domTextMap`). Offsets map through `textRangeToSource` / `sourceRangeToText` only when both texts are equal; otherwise only the quote is used.
- Creating (admin): selection inside one text element of one block (else a notice). The field element is matched to a data leaf by its text (n-th equal text = n-th equal leaf). With a live room (`collabClient.getDoc()`), pending typing is flushed first and the positions are encoded on the leaf's Y.Text; without one (collaboration off, `disableCollaboration`, a positional field before its key exists, read-only rooms are fine) the anchor is the quote (+ path from the block's saved data).
- Finding: relative positions in the current room doc (must resolve to the same Y.Text, non-empty), then the best quote match (prefix/suffix score) among the block's text elements, else `changed` ("Text changed", the thread stays on its block); a missing block is `detached` as before. One save that rewrites text on both sides of a range (one diff region per text) drops the positions; the quote then finds the text if it still exists.
- Painting: CSS Custom Highlight API `mex-comment` (open threads) and `mex-comment-active` (the thread the caret is in or that was jumped to), styles in `tools/styles.js`; a page-wide registry merges the ranges of all fields; the Editor.js DOM is never changed. Browsers without the API show no highlight (threads and markers still work).

Mentions (`shared/comment-mentions.mjs`, `services/comment-notifications.js`):

- Body stays plain text (`normalizeCommentBody`). Picking a person inserts `@<name>`; the client sends the ids whose `@<name>` is still in the text (`mentionsInText`). The server resolves the ids (active, not blocked admins), keeps only people whose own ability has `access` + `comments.read` and passes `access.checkField` (CM read on document, locale, field; identity incl. `fieldKey`), and stores their admin ids in the comment's `mentions` JSON column (max 20, never returned). Names are read live; a deleted admin's id no longer resolves (the text stays). The admin renders `@<name>` of listed people as chips (`mentionSegments`, `you` styled apart).
- Picker: active admins except the caller matching `q` on first name, last name or username (never e-mail), 25 candidates checked, 8 returned; `comments.mentionsPerMinute` (default 60) searches per admin (counter `mentions:<adminId>`, 429).

Notifications:

- Hidden content type `plugin::magic-editor-x.comment-notification` (table `magic_editor_comment_notifications`): `recipientId`, `kind` (`mention`|`reply`), `commentId`, `threadId`, `contentType`, `entryId`, `entryLocale`, `fieldName` (field identity), `blockId`, `readAt`, `emailedAt`. Ids only, no text. One row per recipient and comment; `mention` for newly mentioned people (also on edit; removed mentions delete their row), `reply` for the thread's other participants (root author, reply authors, people mentioned in the thread), never the author, at most 50 recipients, each re-checked like mentions.
- Listing (`notification`): `{ id, kind, read, createdAt, threadId, actor: { name, deleted }, snippet (comment text, one line, max 200), excerpt (thread excerpt), target: { kind: 'collectionType'|'singleType', uid, documentId, locale, field, fieldKey, typeName, title } }`. The newest 200 rows are scanned and each is checked against the caller's current access (rows of documents they can no longer read are hidden, not deleted). `title` is the Content Manager main field when the caller may read it, else null.
- Retention (same rules as comments): deleted with the comment (a thread root takes its thread's), with the entry locale (`removeForEntries`), and when the recipient admin is deleted (`anonymizeUser` lifecycle). Rows around the Document Service are not cleaned up.
- Admin: the comments panel shows "You were mentioned in N threads" / "New replies …" with "Mark as read", and per thread "Mentioned you" / "New reply". Homepage widget "Mentions and replies" (`app.widgets.register`, Strapi 5.13+, permissions `access` + `comments.read`; `components/MentionsWidget`): newest 5, unread count, mark read/unread, mark all read, polling every 60 s while the tab is visible and on focus. Links go to the Content Manager edit view with `plugins[i18n][locale]` and `mexThread=<threadId>` (`MentionsWidget/link.mjs`); the field that holds that thread opens its panel, focuses the thread (shows resolved threads for it) and marks its notifications read.

E-mail (opt-in): `comments.notifications.email` (default `false`) sends mention e-mails through `strapi.plugin('email').service('email').send` after the response (never blocks or fails the comment), at most `comments.notifications.emailPerHour` (default 10) per recipient (counter `mentionmail:<adminId>`). Content: "<name> mentioned you in a comment on "<title>" (<type>)" (title only when the recipient may read it) and the absolute admin link (`admin.absoluteUrl`); never the comment text. English only (the server has no admin locale of the recipient). Subject and names are header-safe (control characters, line and paragraph separators and bidi overrides removed, bounded); the address must match a strict single-address pattern; no `from`/`replyTo` from user input (the email plugin's defaults). An escaped HTML part is always sent (Strapi's nodemailer provider would otherwise send the text as HTML). Settings > Configuration shows the state read-only (`environment.mentionEmails: { enabled, available, perHour }`).

Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+M comments on the selection (also in read-only editors, which show a floating "Comment" button next to the selection; the inline toolbar has "Comment" for editors, tool key `comment$mex`), Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+N / Shift: next / previous open comment (its text becomes active and the thread is focused); clicking commented text shows its thread without moving focus. In the comment boxes `@` opens the picker (combobox: arrows, Enter/Tab picks, Escape closes the list), Ctrl/Cmd+Enter posts and is stopped there (Strapi 5.61's edit view saves on Ctrl/Cmd+Enter).

Audit: `comment.mention` (`counts.mentions`, `meta.threadId`, block id) when new mention notifications were created; recipients are not recorded.

Tests: `tests/comment-anchors.test.mjs`, `tests/comment-mentions.test.mjs`, `tests/integration/comment-mentions.test.mjs` (`MEX_MAIL_LOG` + `MEX_MAIL_EXPECTED=on|off` for the e-mail case against a fake SMTP server).

## Synced blocks (2.3)

- Source: a row of `plugin::magic-editor-x.template` with `kind: 'synced'` (same fields, limits, sanitising, scope, `enabled`, order and `templates.manage` permission as templates and patterns; managed on Settings > Templates with the kind filter). Chosen over a content type of its own because the stored shape, validation, settings UI and permission are identical; the differences are kind-specific branches in `services/templates.js`. Rules: a source never contains a `synced` block (400 `fieldErrors.blocks` "A synced block cannot contain another synced block"; the admin form checks it too), so references cannot nest or form cycles; the kind of a source never changes and a template/pattern never becomes a source (400 `fieldErrors.kind`); `enabled: false` only stops offering it for insertion (`GET /templates/:id` still returns it, references keep rendering it). Sources are not localised and have no Draft & Publish: a saved change is live in published output at once (that is the point of the feature).
- Field value: block `{ type: 'synced', data: { ref: <source documentId> } }`, nothing else (policy: invalid refs become `''`; schema `data_synced`; types `SyncedData`). Stored as `{ ref, _mex: 1 }` (built-in marker, see Media Library blocks > Compatibility): a pre-2.3 custom block named `synced` keeps the generic policy and its own tool; new custom blocks cannot use the name. Presets: in `full` and `article`, not in `basic`/`minimal`; `allowedBlocks` may list it; `checkPreset` reports `BLOCK_NOT_ALLOWED`. The Yjs guard refuses a built-in synced block whose data is not exactly `{ ref, _mex? }` with a documentId (or `''`). `computeStats` counts no text for it (limits count the reference as one block).
- Expansion (`shared/synced.mjs` `expandSynced(data, lookup, { filter, maxBlocks, maxBytes })`): each reference is replaced by a deep copy of the source blocks with ids `<refBlockId>-<sourceBlockId>` (hashed when longer than 64 characters, unique in the document); references inside a source are dropped; toggle `items` counts of enclosing toggles are recomputed (`replaceBlocks`, `toBlockTree`/`fromBlockTree`); a missing source, a source with no allowed block, or one that would exceed 5000 blocks / ~5 MiB expands to nothing. `origins` maps copied ids to the reference.
- Preset interaction (decided: filter, not refuse): `templates.mjs` `filterSyncedForField(blocks, preset)` leaves out blocks of types the containing field does not allow (a disallowed toggle's content stays), fixes heading levels and links like "Fix automatically", leaves out unfixable blocks and images without alt in `requireAlt` fields. Refusing the field save was rejected because a source can change after the field was saved. The editor view shows "N blocks of the source are not allowed in this field and left out".
- Content API / GraphQL (`services/references.js` `expandAll`, before reference collection): one query for all sources of a response (`templates.syncedSources(ids)`, at most `SYNCED_LIMITS.refsPerResponse` = 100 distinct sources), each source cleaned with the containing field's sanitiser (`cleanEditorValue` with the configured `rawHtml` and the preset's inline tags) and filtered by its preset (`render-output.js` and `graphql.js` pass `attribute.options`). Permission model: sources are shared editorial content an author embedded on purpose, so they are expanded for every caller who can read the containing entry; internal links, mentions, embedded entries and media inside them are resolved with the caller's permissions like any other reference (unreadable targets become plain text / `null`). `json` output has the copied blocks inline with `syncedFrom: <ref>`; without `?mex` the stored reference is returned unchanged.
- Renderers: option `synced` (`{ [ref]: document | blocks }`, a `Map`, or `(ref) => document | blocks | null`) in `renderHtml`/`renderText`/`renderMarkdown`/`renderTree` and the React/Vue components (`prepareBlocks` expands before cleaning, so the copies are cleaned and rendered like any block and a `toc` lists their headings); without it, or for an unknown ref, a synced block renders nothing.
- Usage (`GET /templates/:id/usage`, `templates.usage`): a bounded scan of the stored data (every `api::` type with editor fields, top level/components/dynamic zones, drafts and published versions, all locales, batches of 100 by id; `USAGE_LIMITS` 200,000 rows / 20 s, then `complete: false`) plus templates/patterns that contain the reference. A scan instead of an index table: it reads what is stored, so edits through the Content Manager, the Content API, scripts or imports are all counted, without write hooks on publish, discard, delete or locale operations. Counts only.
- History: versions store the reference only; restoring restores the reference; old versions render the current source (like a component). The diff shows "Synced block <name>" (`syncedDiffRefs`; `leafKind` treats `ref` as a value). Source versions are kept since 2.4 (see "Audit trail, synced source versions and the link check").
- Admin: tool `tools/synced.js` (no toolbox entry; inserted from the "Insert template" dialog's "Synced blocks" section, offered only where the preset allows `synced`; `GET /templates?uid&field` filters them). The tool hands its `data-mutation-free` element to the field (`config.mount`), which renders `SyncedBlockView` through a React portal: "Synced block: <name>", the source rendered with `RenderedContent` after `filterSyncedForField`, "Edit source" (`LinkButton isExternal` to `/settings/magic-editor-x/templates?edit=<id>`, only with `templates.manage`), "Detach" (editors: the reference is replaced by a copy through `prepareInsertion` and `replaceContent`, fresh ids, one undo step), "Synced block removed" when the source is gone (404). Sources load through `editor/synced-store.js` (one cache per page, shared requests, refresh on focus/visibility, every 30 s while visible, `MAX_AGE_MS` 15 s). The in-field preview passes the sources as `options.synced`. Keydown on the view's controls does not reach Editor.js.

## Block suggestions and review workflows (2.4)

Reviewers propose block changes; editors accept or reject them. Block level only: Editor.js 2.x keeps no change marks in its saved data and every tool owns its DOM, so character-level track changes are out of reach; a suggestion is one whole proposed block, shown with the word diff of `shared/diff.mjs`.
